newsitem.title: UK: Ford asks UK govt for aid to save plant-paper.
newsitem.headline: Ford asks UK govt for aid to save plant-paper.

text.p: Ford Motor Co, the U.S. car giant which announced 1,300 job cuts at its Halewood plant in Liverpool last week, is set to ask the UK government for 75 million stg in aid to help prevent the threat of full closure in future, said a report in the Sunday Times newspaper.
The report said Ford warned unless it got funding to develop the new vehicle the entire Halewood plant could close losing a further 2,500 Ford jobs in future, as well as hitting suppliers.
The car-manufacturer devastated its UK work force last week by telling them that 1,300 jobs would have to go as the group planned to make the new Escort car model in continental Europe.
Halewood in northwest England has been given a vague promise of making a new vehicle once production of the current Escort model ends in three years.

The report said that Jac Nasser, head of Ford's global automotive operations and a former chairman of Ford of Europe, put the Halewood proposal to Ian Lang, the government's president of the board of trade last Thursday -- the day the job cuts were announced.
Government officials were reported to be looking at the proposal and are due to make a decision next week.
Ford has indicated that the new vehicle -- which could be a people carrier van -- will only go ahead if it gets the government aid and if trade unions back the restructuring plans.
But to date unions including the Transport and General Workers Union, have rejected proposals and are threatening possible strike action.
The reason for the UK shake-up is severe over-capacity in a highly competitive market which has seen industry margins come under pressure from price discounting in an effort to boost sales.
